concept.text: A proof that every simply connected, closed three-manifold is homeomorphic to the three-sphere. Proved by Grigori Perelman (2002–2003); the Clay Institute awarded the Millennium Prize in 2010, which he declined. Sources given: https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/ ; https://world-of-mathematics.com/blog/millennium-problems-overview/.

page.title: Proof of the Poincaré conjecture
page.definition: A proof that every closed, simply connected 3-manifold is homeomorphic to S³, the unit sphere in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A 3-manifold is locally like ordinary 3-space; closed means compact without boundary, simply connected means connected with every loop contractible, and homeomorphic means related by a continuous bijection with continuous inverse.

goal.need: An algorithm can recognize the 3-sphere from a triangulation. Homology alone leaves an ambiguity: one closed 3-manifold has the sphere’s homology groups but has 120 distinct classes of based loops up to continuous deformation. The proof lets a topologist identify a closed 3-manifold as the sphere as soon as every loop is known to contract, whatever its geometry. Manifolds with nontrivial fundamental group require further classification.

statements.quote: to emphasize the importance of working towards a solution of the deepest, most difficult problems

statements.quote: The Poincaré conjecture is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems established by CMI in 2000.
statements.context: Clay announced the seven problems in Paris on 24 May 2000 and recalled the designation in its announcement of the prize for Perelman.

completion.title: A confirmed proof identifies every closed, simply connected topological 3-manifold with S³ up to homeomorphism.
completion.criterion: Prove that every closed, simply connected topological 3-manifold is homeomorphic to S³. Confirmation requires a proof accepted by the mathematical community or a proof of the same statement checked in a proof assistant. In dimension three, a proof that every closed, smooth, simply connected manifold is diffeomorphic to S³ suffices because every topological 3-manifold admits a smooth structure.
completion.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute’s official problem description by John Milnor specifies the theorem. Confirmation follows the mathematical community’s convention of proof.
completion.threshold_quote: every simply connected closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere
completion.basis: Morgan and Tian’s 2007 monograph gives the detailed argument following Perelman. Clay announced its award on 18 March 2010 after independent scrutiny, recommendations from its advisory committees and a decision by its Board of Directors. That ruling documents acceptance. Clay’s two-year publication interval is a prize eligibility rule.

milestones.title: Every closed 3-manifold with positive Ricci curvature admits a metric of constant positive curvature.
milestones.criterion: Prove that every smooth closed 3-manifold admitting a Riemannian metric with strictly positive Ricci curvature also admits a metric with constant positive sectional curvature. For a simply connected manifold, this identifies the manifold with S³.
milestones.set_by: Hamilton, Main Theorem 1.1 in Three-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature (1982); the field's convention of establishing a theorem by proof.
milestones.threshold_quote: Then X also admits a metric of constant positive curvature.

milestones.title: Ricci flow on a closed manifold cannot collapse locally at a finite singular time.
milestones.criterion: For any smooth Ricci flow g(t) on a closed n-manifold over 0 ≤ t < T < ∞, rule out sequences tₖ → T and metric balls Bₖ of radius rₖ at time tₖ for which rₖ²/tₖ stays bounded, |Rm| ≤ rₖ⁻² throughout Bₖ, and Vol(Bₖ)/rₖⁿ → 0. Rm is the Riemann curvature tensor. Distances, volumes and curvature in each ball are measured at tₖ.
milestones.set_by: Perelman, no local collapsing theorem, §4.1 (2002), developed in Morgan and Tian's CMI/AMS exposition (2007); the field's proof convention.
milestones.threshold_quote: If $M$ is closed and $T<\infty,$ then $g_{ij}(t)$ is not locally collapsing at $T.$

milestones.title: Every closed oriented 3-manifold admits Ricci flow with surgery for all t ≥ 0.
milestones.criterion: For every smooth closed oriented 3-manifold with any initial Riemannian metric, construct a Ricci flow with surgery for all t ≥ 0, allowing an empty manifold after extinction. Only finitely many surgeries may occur in a bounded time interval. At a surgery time the topological changes are connected-sum decompositions and removal of components diffeomorphic to S² × S¹, to ℝP³ # ℝP³, or to a manifold admitting constant positive sectional curvature.
milestones.set_by: Perelman, §5.1 (2003); Morgan and Tian, Theorem 0.3 (2007), whose hypothesis includes all closed oriented 3-manifolds; the field's proof convention.
milestones.threshold_quote: The topological change in the 3-manifold as one crosses a surgery time is a connected sum decomposition together with removal of connected components

milestones.title: Surgery flow becomes extinct in finite time on closed oriented 3-manifolds with no aspherical prime factor.
milestones.criterion: For every initial Riemannian metric on a closed oriented 3-manifold whose prime decomposition contains no aspherical factor, prove that there is a finite T such that the manifold in the Ricci flow with surgery is empty for every t ≥ T. Prime decomposition expresses the manifold as a connected sum. An aspherical factor has contractible universal cover. The hypotheses include every closed simply connected 3-manifold.
milestones.set_by: Perelman, Theorem 1.1 (2003); Morgan and Tian, Theorem 0.4 (2007), with their 2015 correction; the field's proof convention.
milestones.threshold_quote: Then for any initial metric on $M$ the solution to the Ricci flow with surgery becomes extinct in finite time.

milestones.title: Rescaled high-curvature neighborhoods in three-dimensional Ricci flow are ε-close to ancient κ-solutions.
milestones.criterion: For ε, κ > 0 and a decreasing φ tending to zero at infinity, prove there is r₀ > 0 with the following property. Consider a smooth Ricci flow on a closed 3-manifold with curvature operator Rm ≥ −φ(R)R and κ-noncollapse on scales below r₀, where R is scalar curvature. At each (x₀,t₀) with t₀ ≥ 1 and Q = R(x₀,t₀) ≥ r₀⁻², rescale by Q. On the ball of original radius (εQ)⁻¹ᐟ² measured at t₀, over the preceding time interval of length (εQ)⁻¹, the rescaled flow must be ε-close to the corresponding region of an ancient κ-solution as defined in §11.1.
milestones.set_by: Perelman, Theorem 12.1 of The entropy formula for the Ricci flow and its geometric applications.
milestones.threshold_quote: after scaling by the factor $Q,$ $\epsilon$-close to the corresponding subset of some ancient solution, satisfying the assumptions in 11.1.

not_found: No statement was found from a mathematical society or prize body disputing the value or feasibility of proving the conjecture.
